title: SB Energy does SoftBank's spadework for Son's AI drive
source_used: Nikkei Asia (opening paragraph and picture caption only; the rest is behind a subscription)
key_facts: Nikkei Asia's sub-headline says the Japanese investor, known for venture bets, is turning to costly infrastructure.
Residents of Piketon, Ohio, a village of 2,000, gathered in August to hear plans to turn a former uranium enrichment plant site into a natural gas-fired power complex.
The complex would supply electricity directly to what would be one of the world's largest data center campuses.
A picture caption shows SoftBank Group chief Masayoshi Son and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick at a March groundbreaking for SB Energy's new data center in Piketon, Ohio.
quote_evidence: Residents of Piketon, Ohio, a village of 2,000 people, gathered in August to hear about plans to transform the site of a former uranium enrichment plant into a natural gas-fired power complex, supplying electricity directly to what would be one of the world’s largest data center campuses.
why_it_matters_hint: SoftBank is moving from venture bets into heavy energy and data center infrastructure through SB Energy.
notes: Only the opening paragraph was readable (about 600 characters, subscription wall); no other outlet carries this feature. Cost, funding and timetable are not visible. Treated as partly verified, so verified_text is false.
